title: How it works
text:
Reading the numbers

Growth is Google’s rising percentage: how much more the query was searched in this window than in the period of the same length just before it. Breakout means more than +5,000%.
Windows shows in which of the three windows (1h, 4h, 24h) the query was rising. A query rising in all three is a sustained story, not a one-off spike.
Fit is an opinion, not a fact. Check the Everything rising table for ideas the scoring missed.

title: Trend radar
text:
Best ideas right now
Queries from the latest run that worked, with a channel-fit score of 40 or more. Fit is scored once per query; growth is Google’s “rising” percentage compared with the previous period of the same length.

title: Trend radar
section: Ideas that keep coming back (last 7 days)
text:
Ideas that keep coming back (last 7 days)
Queries seen in two or more runs. A query that stays on the rising list for days is usually a bigger story than a one-hour spike.

title: Trend radar
section: Everything rising in the latest run
text:
Everything rising in the latest run
All rising queries, including the ones that are not a fit, so you can spot what the scoring missed. Use the search box to filter by window or seed.

title: Run health
text: Google Trends sometimes refuses automated requests with HTTP 429 (“too many requests”). A run where most searches show rate_limited was blocked; the next run usually works. If this happens for several runs in a row, increase the pauses in run_radar.R or remove seeds from seeds.txt.
